STATUS: ANSWER
Hard filtering flags variants by applying predefined thresholds to variant annotations, such as allele depth and mapping quality; variants that fail any criterion are flagged [sarek_vc_theory#h008]. It is mostly useful when calling a few samples and enough data are not available for more sophisticated solutions [sarek_vc_theory#h008]. The Sarek tutorial applies VQSR after variant calling [sarek_vc_sarek#h007]. Its tutorial dataset is small, so some annotations have insufficient data or no variance, and the filtering options were changed and limited to a subset of annotations [sarek_vc_sarek#h007]. The observations do not state a general rule for choosing hard filtering over VQSR.
